standard_prerequisites.name: The criterion that a submodule of an injective module is injective exactly when it has no nontrivial essential extension inside it
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked at the start of the counted proof (source line 563)
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces injectivity of the power-torsion submodule to the absence of essential extensions.

core_obligations: (1): assuming a strictly larger submodule and an element outside the torsion part, use Noetherianity to write the annihilator ideal of that element as finitely generated, find a power of the multiplier annihilating all the generators applied to the element, and show that the resulting element generates a submodule meeting the torsion part trivially, contradicting essentialness (proof lines 563-582)

(2): write the ideal as finitely generated and express the power-torsion submodule as an iterated power-torsion submodule with respect to the generators, then apply (1) and induction (proof lines 583-587)
proof_roadmap: (1)：设 E ⊂ E' 本质且取 x ∈ E' ∖ E，令 J = {a : ax ∈ E}；由 Noether 性 J = (g_1,…,g_t)，取 n 使 f^{n_i}g_i x = 0，令 n = max n_i，则 x' = f^n x 满足 Ann(x') = J ⇒ Rx' ∩ E = 0 ⇒ E' 不本质，矛盾。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that for an injective module over a Noetherian ring the submodule of elements annihilated by a power of a single element, and more generally the power-torsion submodule of an ideal, are injective (author lemma at source lines 552-561, label lemma-injective-module-divide). The proof (source lines 563-588) uses the essential-extension criterion, argues with the annihilator ideal made finitely generated by Noetherianity to produce an element meeting the torsion part trivially, and reduces the ideal case to the single-element case by iteration (proof lines 563-587). The annihilator argument is the substance. H3.
